contract: main_case_2026_10_14 item_job_capital.cjs (the v7 brief): lines, by_generation, factor, per_wage_dollar, central_bn, arms, gates
frame: the identified union (39,712,493 on audit row 4's weights), CPS ASEC 2025 wage and salary income (WSAL_VAL) by the longest job's industry, the case's fill-in correction split by generation; no status rules: an off-books job's capital is taxed at its source whether or not the wage is reported (the case's production term also counts all CPS earnings)

conventions.readings: low = the band's low end (corporate at 1), high = its high end (corporate at the normal-return share); every line's response is {low, high}
conventions.group_bn: the union's target before the response, key_share x national_bn, $bn (taxes on the capital that serves its jobs)
conventions.item_bn: response x group_bn at each reading: the taxes a removal loses; central_bn sums the lines and net_cost_change_bn is minus it
conventions.plain_wage_share: the union's share of the case's wage key (corporate_labor at cbo_collective on the September 29 payload model, case_keys.json case_wage_key); lane_plain_wage_share is the union's share of all CPS wages here
conventions.factor: a group's key share over its share of the case's wage key (union, G1, G2, G3plus: case_wage_key.shares) or over its plain wage share on this lane's frame (white_nh, black_nh: third-plus non-Hispanic white and Black alone; *_all: every nativity); by_generation[G] = factor[G] x case share of G x national_bn
conventions.by_generation: the union's generations' targets before the response, convention a; they add to group_bn
conventions.national_bn: the case's line: corporate = corporate_capital + corporate_labor, business_property = remaining_production_property, other_production_taxes the whole line; base_bn is the part the key spreads (mining's cells out of every line; other production taxes: the residential parts of documentary taxes and special assessments out as well)

label: the lane's central reading: every line by industry at the union's share of each industry's CPS wage bill, mining at 0

se_bn.rule: SDR over the 160 replicate weights (the CPS sample); fill_in from the fill-in rel_change SE

per_wage_dollar.rule: tax lost at the line's response per dollar of the group's CPS wage and salary income on this lane's frame (all wages, row 4 and the fill-in; the employer_hi key's wage concept, WSAL_VAL), by reading; all sums the lines; national is the item's bases over national CPS wages

responses_rule.mining: 0 on every line at both readings (its cells carry no tax in the key)
responses_rule.rule: business property = tau + (1 - tau) x r_b: r_b = 1 - lambda_b (1 - delta_L) on the real property, the tangible personal property part tau leaving whole; corporate leaves whole at the low end and only its normal-return share at the high end

normal_return.source: Treasury OTA Technical Paper 5 (Cronin, Lin, Power and Cooper, May 2012), p. 7: "we find that 63 percent of current corporate taxable income is due to supernormal returns" and "the remaining 37 percent of the corporate tax on the taxable income attributable to normal returns"
normal_return.ota_2021: Treasury OTA, Treasury's Distribution Methodology and Results (July 2021; Summary-of-OTA-Distribution-Methodology-05102021.pdf), p. 3 note 4: "split between capital income (81.5 percent) and labor income (18.5 percent)"

power_frerick.source: Power and Frerick, Have Excess Returns To Corporations Been Increasing Over Time?, Treasury OTA Working Paper 111 (November 2016; National Tax Journal 69(4), 2016): abstract p. 2, the risk-free share of the C corporation base "averaging 40 percent from 1992-2002 and 25 percent from 2003-2013"; Table 1 p. 16, three-year averages 2011-2013 by industry

normal_return.fox_2020: beside, no arm: Fox, Does Capital Bear the U.S. Corporate Tax After All?, Journal of Empirical Legal Studies 17(1), 2020, p. 72: actual 1995-2013 revenue exceeded a hypothetical cash-flow tax's by "about 4 percent on average" (21 percent under more conservative assumptions, note 5)
normal_return.what_supernormal_includes: Power and Frerick p. 4: returns above the risk-free rate "including returns to risk, entrepreneurial labor, decreasing returns to scale, market power, luck, etc."; most self-created intangibles are already expensed (Appendix A p. 21), so their returns sit in the excess part

mining.rule: excluded from the key: its cells carry no tax on any line (the team lead, 2026-10-14); the arm mining_as_other_industries keeps them

other_production_line.key_rule: key_share = the union's tax on the base over the whole case line: the residential parts and mining's cells give the group no share, which leaves them at zero as v6 does
other_production_line.residential_rule: beside, outside the item: the residential parts of documentary and stamp taxes and special assessments (Z.1 residential share) split owner / tenant by Z.1 market value, at the case's owner and tenant property keys and v6's responses for those lines

case_wage_key.rule: the union's and each generation's share of corporate_labor's wage key at cbo_collective on the September 29 payload model (main_case_2026_10_07/package.cjs SEPT29; generations from generation_account_2026_09_24 model_<G>.json with generation_corrections_sept29.json payloads.a): target over the line's national

mining_as_other_industries.label: mining's three taxes respond as other industries' do (the build before 2026-10-14)

normal_return_share.label: corporate at TP-5's normal-return share (0.37) at both readings

normal_return_share_0_25.label: the high reading's corporate response at Power and Frerick's 2003-2013 normal-return share (Treasury OTA Working Paper 111, abstract)

normal_return_share_by_industry.label: the high reading's corporate response at each industry's normal-return share (Power and Frerick Table 1, 2011-2013), as the union's personal effective share
normal_return_share_by_industry.note: one response for every group and allocation; each group's own effective share is in effective_high_corporate_response

plain_wage_share.label: the plain wage share in place of the industry key: every line's base at each group's share of all CPS wages on this lane's frame
plain_wage_share.note: the base that responds (mining and the residential parts out); the receipt lane's ceiling on the case's frame is minus plain_wage_share x the three lines' national, every line at 1

foreign_source_removed.label: federal tax on foreign-source corporate income removed from the corporate base (IRS SOI TY2021)

business_land_at_0.label: business land at response 0: the land part of business property tax stays

business_land_at_1.label: business land at response 1: the whole business property tax leaves

floor.label: the floor: CBO's labour share of corporate tax only, at the case's wage key; the other lines at response 0
floor.note: corporate base 25% of the whole corporate national (corporate_labor's 165.92125bn), mining included

case_wage_key.label: the case's wage key (the status rules at the on-books lane's shares) in place of all CPS wages: each generation's targets times its share of the case's wage key over its plain share on this lane's frame
case_wage_key.note: [INFERENCE] the off-books wages take each generation's own industry mix
